headline: Remote Backcountry Registration for Sahtu Wilderness
reservation: All visitors must register with Parks Canada prior to entering this remote wilderness area, as there are no established roads or staffed entry booths within the park. While entry registration is separate from specific mountaineering or river outfitting requirements, travelers should verify the latest public safety protocols with the park office in Tulita or Norman Wells. Changing seasonal management and wildlife protection zones mean travelers must confirm current access through official channels before departing.

days.title: Sacred Peaks and Mountain Headwaters
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Norman Wells via chartered floatplane

stops.name: Mount Nááts'įhch'oh
stops.detail: Observe the distinct pointed peak that gives the park its name and serves as a significant spiritual landmark for the Shúta Got’ine.

stops.name: Nááts'įhch'oh Tué (Moose Ponds)
stops.detail: Explore the wetlands at the headwaters of the South Nahanni River, known for its distinct karst topography and resident wildlife.

days.driving: Allow 1–2 hours for chartered air transfer; conditions vary
days.note: Travel is dependent on bush plane availability and weather visibility over the Mackenzie Mountains.

days.title: Thermal Waters and Ancient Geology
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from high-elevation backcountry camp

stops.name: Shúho̧t’inȩ Tué (Hot Springs)

stops.name: Broken Skull River

days.driving: Local backcountry walking or paddling; conditions vary
days.note: River levels fluctuate rapidly based on summer snowmelt and regional rainfall.

days.title: High Alpine Tundra Exploration
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Broken Skull valley

stops.name: Griz Bar
stops.detail: Utilize this common gravel bar landing site for access to expansive tundra hiking and mountain vistas.

stops.name: Tȩȩ˛tú̧ (Little Dal Lake)
stops.detail: Venture toward the park boundary to see the vibrant blue waters framed by dramatic limestone cliffs.

days.driving: Local bush plane transfer or rugged hiking; conditions vary
days.note: Allow ample time for bush plane pickups, which may be delayed by regional smoke or low cloud ceilings.

intel.title: Airbase Logistics
intel.text: There are no parking lots within the park; long-term parking is typically arranged at private air charter bases in Norman Wells or Tulita. Travelers should verify security and fees with their specific flight provider before arrival.

intel.title: Satellite Dependency
intel.text: Mobile coverage is non-existent within the park boundaries and throughout most of the Sahtu region. Satellite communication devices are the standard for backcountry safety and emergency check-ins.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: Fuel for stoves or expedition equipment must be secured in Norman Wells before chartering into the park. There are no retail services or supply depots once you depart the gateway towns.

intel.title: Summer Window
intel.text: The travel season is limited to July and August when the high-altitude lakes are free of ice. Early September brings a high probability of snow which can complicate air extraction.

intel.title: Charter Access Only
intel.text: Access is almost exclusively by floatplane or ski-plane as there is no road network connecting to the park. Hikers arriving via the Canol Heritage Trail must be prepared for extremely strenuous self-supported travel.

plan.arrival: Landing at Norman Wells (YVQ), check in with the Parks Canada office for a mandatory safety briefing, then coordinate with your pre-booked air charter for the flight into the reserve.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles cannot reach the park; transport is limited to specialized bush planes. Check with air carriers regarding strict weight limits for gear.
plan.goldenHour: Mount Nááts'įhch'oh viewpoint during the long summer twilight, noting that sun angles remain high until late evening.
